---
<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{assum:generators}
		$\mathscr{H}=\mathbb{C}^d$ with $2\le d<\infty$; $H=H^\ast\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$; $L\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$; $A=A^\ast\in M_{d^2}(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies \eqref{eq:A-symmetry}. No boundedness clause is imposed as a restriction: it holds by $d<\infty$.
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:commutator}
		$\|[B,\rho]\|_1\le2\|B\|_\infty\|\rho\|_1$ for $B,\rho\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Triangle inequality and $\|B\rho\|_1\le\|B\|_\infty\|\rho\|_1$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:partial-trace}
		For $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{H}\otimes\mathscr{H})$ and $\delta\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$, $\|\operatorname{Tr}_2(A(1\otimes\delta))\|_\infty\le\|A\|_\infty\|\delta\|_1$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
For unit vectors $\phi,\psi$, $|\langle\phi,\operatorname{Tr}_2(A(1\otimes\delta))\psi\rangle|=|\operatorname{Tr}(A(|\psi\rangle\langle\phi|\otimes\delta))|\le\|A\|_\infty\||\psi\rangle\langle\phi|\otimes\delta\|_1=\|A\|_\infty\|\delta\|_1$, using that the trace norm factorises over tensor products. Take the supremum over $\phi,\psi$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:pt-calculus}
		Let $Y\in\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{H}^{\otimes N})$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(PT1)] If $X$ acts on kept factors only, $\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}((X\otimes1)Y)=X\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}Y$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}(Y(X\otimes1))=(\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}Y)X$.
			\item[(PT2)] The partial trace over a factor is cyclic with respect to operators acting on that factor alone.
			\item[(PT3)] If $X$ acts on factor $j\notin S$ only, then $\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}(X_jY)$ depends on $Y$ only through $\Gamma^{(S\cup\{j\})}$: with $j$ in the last slot, $\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}(X_jY)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{last}}((1\otimes\cdots\otimes X)\Gamma^{(S\cup\{j\})})$, and likewise for right multiplication.
			\item[(PT4)] $\operatorname{Tr}_2((\rho\otimes\sigma)A)=\rho\,\mathsf{B}(\sigma)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_2(A(\rho\otimes\sigma))=\mathsf{B}(\sigma)\rho$, hence $\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\rho\otimes\sigma]=[\mathsf{B}(\sigma),\rho]$.
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
All four follow from the duality $\operatorname{Tr}(Z\operatorname{Tr}_{S^c}Y)=\operatorname{Tr}((Z\otimes1)Y)$ and the definition \eqref{eq:ops} of $\mathsf{B}$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:reference}
		Let $\gamma_0=|\psi_0\rangle\langle\psi_0|\in\mathcal S$ be pure and deterministic. The system
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:reference}
			d\gamma_{j,t}=\big(-i[H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),\gamma_{j,t}]+\mathcal{D}\gamma_{j,t}\big)dt+\mathcal{M}[\gamma_{j,t}]\,dB_j(t),\qquad \gamma_{j,0}=\gamma_0,\quad \eta_t:=\mathbb{E}\gamma_{1,t},
		\end{equation}
		$j=1,\dots,N$, has a unique solution in $\mathcal C_{ad}([0,T];M_d(\mathbb{C}))^N$ with values in $\mathcal S$. Moreover:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(a)] $\gamma_{1,\cdot},\dots,\gamma_{N,\cdot}$ are independent and identically distributed, and $\gamma_{j,t}=|\phi_{j,t}\rangle\langle\phi_{j,t}|$ is a rank-one projection for every $t$, with
			\begin{equation}\label{eq:reference-vector}
				d\phi_{j,t}=\Big(-i\big(H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t)\big)-\tfrac12\big(L^\ast L-\nu_{j,t}L+\tfrac14\nu_{j,t}^2\big)\Big)\phi_{j,t}\,dt+\Big(L-\tfrac{\nu_{j,t}}2\Big)\phi_{j,t}\,dB_j(t),
			\end{equation}
			$\nu_{j,t}=\langle\phi_{j,t},(L+L^\ast)\phi_{j,t}\rangle$, $\phi_{j,0}=\psi_0$;
			\item[(b)] $\eta$ is deterministic, does not depend on $N$, and is the unique solution of the Hartree--Lindblad equation
			\begin{equation}\label{eq:hartree}
				\dot\eta_t=-i\big[H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),\eta_t\big]+\mathcal{D}\eta_t,\qquad \eta_0=\gamma_0.
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The case $j=1$, in which $\eta=\mathbb{E}\gamma_1$ is determined self-consistently, is Theorem \ref{thm:wellposed} below, whose contraction estimate uses only $\|\mathbb{E} X\|_1\le\mathbb{E}\|X\|_1$ and Lemmas \ref{lem:commutator}--\ref{lem:partial-trace}; this fixes the deterministic path $\eta$. For $j\ge2$ the equation is then \eqref{eq:mild} with $B_j$ in place of $B_1$ and $\eta$ already given, so it is a one-particle Belavkin equation with the bounded time-dependent self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t)$. Given $\eta$, the $N$ equations are decoupled, have identical coefficients and identical initial data, and are driven by independent Brownian motions, which gives (a); the vector form \eqref{eq:reference-vector} and purity are the one-particle case of Proposition \ref{prop:purity-N}. For (b), take expectations in \eqref{eq:reference}: the martingale term has zero mean and $\mathsf{B}(\eta_t)$ is deterministic, so $\eta$ satisfies \eqref{eq:hartree}, which has bounded locally Lipschitz coefficients on the compact set $\mathcal S$ and hence a unique solution, involving no $N$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- convention-1: body_md -->
\label{conv:coupling}
		Throughout, $\gamma_t:=\gamma_{1,t}$ is the reference filter of the tagged particle, driven by $B_1$ on the same probability space as $\Gamma^N_t$ and with the same initial datum, and
		\[
		F^N_t:=\sqrt N\big(\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_t\big),\qquad
		\widehat{G}^N_t:=\sqrt N\big(\overline\Gamma_t-\eta_t\big).
		\]
<!-- end convention-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:coupling}
		Convention \ref{conv:coupling} is the coupling under which \eqref{eq:KP-rate-trace} is stated in \cite{Kolokoltsov2026}: each $\Gamma^{(j)}$ is compared with the filter driven by the corresponding innovation. At $A=0$ it gives $F^N\equiv0$, which is the correct value for the fluctuation of a conditional state around its own filter: with no interaction there is nothing left to fluctuate, and the whole content of the limit theorem is carried by the interaction.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:variance}
		Let $\gamma_0\in\mathcal S$ be deterministic with $\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]\ne0$. Set $B:=\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]/\|\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]\|_\infty$ and $b_t:=\operatorname{Tr}(B\gamma_t)$. There are $t_0,c_0>0$, depending only on $d,\|H\|_\infty,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty,\gamma_0$, with $\operatorname{Var}(b_t)\ge c_0t$ for $0<t\le t_0$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Write $b_t=b_0+\int_0^ta_s\,ds+\int_0^t\sigma_s\,d\beta_s$ with $a,\sigma$ bounded by a constant $C$ and continuous, and $\sigma_s=\operatorname{Tr}(B\mathcal{M}[\gamma_s])$, so $\sigma_0=\|\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]\|_2^2/\|\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]\|_\infty>0$. With $X_t=\int_0^t(a_s-\mathbb{E} a_s)ds$ and $Y_t=\int_0^t\sigma_s\,d\beta_s$ we have $b_t-\mathbb{E} b_t=X_t+Y_t$ and $(X+Y)^2\ge\tfrac12Y^2-X^2$, so
		$\operatorname{Var}(b_t)\ge\tfrac12\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\sigma_s^2\,ds-4C^2t^2$. By dominated convergence $\mathbb{E}\sigma_s^2\to\sigma_0^2$ as $s\downarrow0$, so $\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\sigma_s^2ds\ge\tfrac{\sigma_0^2}2t$ for small $t$, and the claim holds with $c_0=\sigma_0^2/8$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:refutation}
		Let $A=0$, $\Gamma^N_0=\gamma_0^{\otimes N}$ with $\gamma_0$ pure and $\mathcal{M}[\gamma_0]\ne0$. Write $\Delta^{\mathrm{ms}}_t:=\Gamma^{(1,2)}_t-\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(1)}_t$ and let $\Delta^{(3),\mathrm{ms}}_t$ be the corresponding three-body cumulant formed with $\Gamma^{(1)}$ in place of the individual marginals. Then there are $t_0,c>0$ independent of $N$ such that for $0<t\le t_0$ and all $N\ge2$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(i)] $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{\mathrm{ms}}_t\|_1\ge ct$ and $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{\mathrm{ms}}_t\|_1^2\ge ct$;
			\item[(ii)] $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(3),\mathrm{ms}}_t\|_1\ge ct$;
			\item[(iii)] under the aggregate coupling, in which the comparison filter is driven by $W^{(N)}=N^{-1/2}\sum_jB_j$, there is $N_0$ with $\mathbb{E}\|F^N_t\|_1^2\ge cNt$ for $N\ge N_0$, and $\mathbb{E}[1-\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma_t\Gamma^{(1)}_t)]\ge ct$, so \eqref{eq:KP-rate-trace} fails for the aggregate-coupled comparison state.
		\end{enumerate}
		By contrast $\Delta^{(ij)}_t\equiv0$ and $\Delta^{(ijk)}_t\equiv0$ in this case.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
At $A=0$ with product initial data, $\Gamma^N_t=\bigotimes_j\gamma_{j,t}$ pathwise with $\gamma_{j,\cdot}$ independent copies driven by $B_j$: apply the It\^o product rule to $\bigotimes_j\gamma_{j,t}$; cross-variations between distinct factors vanish by independence of the $B_j$, the drift is the sum of the one-particle drifts on the respective factors, and the coefficient of $dB_j$ is $\gamma_{1,t}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{M}[\gamma_{j,t}]\otimes\cdots\otimes\gamma_{N,t}$, which coincides with the coefficient in \eqref{eq:N-particle} at the product state since $\operatorname{Tr}((L_j+L_j^\ast)\bigotimes_k\gamma_{k,t})=\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\gamma_{j,t})$. Pathwise uniqueness for \eqref{eq:N-particle} identifies the two. Hence $\Gamma^{(1)}_t=\gamma_{1,t}$ and all connected correlations of distinct particles vanish.
		
		Write $b_j(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(B\gamma_{j,t})$ with $B$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:variance}; the $b_j$ are i.i.d.\ with variance at least $c_0t$ and $|b_j|\le1$.
		
		(i) $\Delta^{\mathrm{ms}}_t=\gamma_{1,t}\otimes(\gamma_{2,t}-\gamma_{1,t})$, so $\|\Delta^{\mathrm{ms}}_t\|_1=\|\gamma_{2,t}-\gamma_{1,t}\|_1\ge|Z|$ with $Z=b_2-b_1$, $\mathbb{E} Z=0$, $\mathbb{E} Z^2\ge2c_0t$, $|Z|\le2$; hence $\mathbb{E}|Z|\ge\mathbb{E} Z^2/2\ge c_0t$.
		
		(ii) Substituting the product form, $\Delta^{(3),\mathrm{ms}}_t=\gamma_1\otimes[\gamma_2\otimes(\gamma_3-\gamma_1)-2\gamma_1\otimes(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)]$. Testing against $1\otimes1\otimes B$ gives $Z=b_1-2b_2+b_3$ with $\mathbb{E} Z^2\ge6c_0t$ and $|Z|\le4$, so $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(3),\mathrm{ms}}_t\|_1\ge\mathbb{E} Z^2/4\ge\tfrac32c_0t$.
		
		(iii) Under the aggregate coupling, $\gamma$ solves the one-particle equation driven by $W^{(N)}$, with $d\langle B_1,W^{(N)}\rangle_t=N^{-1/2}dt$. Let $x_t=\operatorname{Tr}(B(\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_t))$; its martingale part is $\int_0^t\sigma^1\,dB_1-\int_0^t\sigma^W dW^{(N)}$ with $\sigma^1_s=\operatorname{Tr}(B\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(1)}_s])$, $\sigma^W_s=\operatorname{Tr}(B\mathcal{M}[\gamma_s])$, so
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\Big(\int_0^t\sigma^1dB_1-\int_0^t\sigma^WdW^{(N)}\Big)^2=\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\big[(\sigma^1_s)^2+(\sigma^W_s)^2\big]ds-2N^{-1/2}\int_0^t\mathbb{E}[\sigma^1_s\sigma^W_s]ds\ \ge\ \sigma_0^2t-2C^2N^{-1/2}t
		\]
		for small $t$, by the argument of Lemma \ref{lem:variance} applied to each flow. For $N\ge N_0:=(4C^2/\sigma_0^2)^2$ the right side is at least $\tfrac{\sigma_0^2}2t$, and as in Lemma \ref{lem:variance}, $\mathbb{E} x_t^2\ge\tfrac{\sigma_0^2}4t-4C^2t^2\ge ct$ for small $t$. Since $|x_t|\le\|\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_t\|_1$, $\mathbb{E}\|F^N_t\|_1^2=N\mathbb{E}\|\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_t\|_1^2\ge N\mathbb{E} x_t^2\ge cNt$. Both states are pure, so $1-\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma_t\Gamma^{(1)}_t)=\tfrac12\|\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_t\|_2^2\ge\tfrac1{2d}x_t^2$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:refutation}
		Items (i)--(ii) say that the two- and three-body defects formed by comparing a marginal of several particles with tensor powers of the \emph{single} marginal $\Gamma^{(1)}$ do not have mean-field order; they are of order $t$ uniformly in $N$, for the trivial reason that distinct particles carry distinct innovations and their states separate at order $\sqrt t$. Item (iii) says the same for the aggregate coupling. The objects that do have mean-field order are the connected correlations \eqref{eq:cumulant2}--\eqref{eq:cumulant3} of distinct particles, and the comparison state is the one driven by the tagged innovation. Both points are already visible at $A=0$, and neither depends on the interaction.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:bdg}
		By Section \ref{ssec:findim}, $(M_d(\mathbb{C}),\|\cdot\|_2)$ is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, so It\^o's isometry and the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality hold in classical form. Transferred to $\|\cdot\|_1$, for predictable square-integrable $\Phi$ and $p\ge2$ there is $C_p=C_p(d)$ with
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:bdg}
			\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\Big\|\int_0^tS_{t-s}\Phi_s\,dB_1(s)\Big\|_1^p\le C_p\,\mathbb{E}\Big(\int_0^T\|\Phi_s\|_1^2\,ds\Big)^{p/2}.
		\end{equation}
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:wellposed}
		Under Assumption \ref{assum:generators}, \eqref{eq:mild} has a unique solution $\gamma^y_\cdot\in\mathcal C_{ad}([0,T];M_d(\mathbb{C}))$ for every $y\in\mathcal S$ and every $T>0$, with values in $\mathcal S$, and there is $C_T$ with
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:lipschitz}
			\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\|\gamma^y_t-\gamma^x_t\|_1^2\le C_T\|y-x\|_1^2,\qquad x,y\in\mathcal S.
		\end{equation}
		If $y$ is pure, $\gamma^y_t$ is pure for every $t$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
\emph{Contraction.} Define $\mathcal P_y$ by the right side of \eqref{eq:mild}. On $\mathcal S$, $|\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\rho)|\le2\|L\|_\infty$, so $\|\mathcal{M}[\gamma]-\mathcal{M}[\tilde\gamma]\|_1\le4\|L\|_\infty\|\gamma-\tilde\gamma\|_1$. For the mean-field drift,
		\[
		\big\|[\mathsf{B}(\mathbb{E}\gamma_s),\gamma_s]-[\mathsf{B}(\mathbb{E}\tilde\gamma_s),\tilde\gamma_s]\big\|_1\le 2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\|\gamma_s-\tilde\gamma_s\|_1+2\|A\|_\infty\|\gamma_s-\tilde\gamma_s\|_1
		\]
		by Lemmas \ref{lem:commutator}--\ref{lem:partial-trace} and $\|\mathbb{E} X\|_1\le\mathbb{E}\|X\|_1$; since $\mathbb{E}\|\gamma_s-\tilde\gamma_s\|_1\le(\mathbb{E}\|\gamma_s-\tilde\gamma_s\|_1^2)^{1/2}$, both terms are controlled by the same weighted norm. Using the semigroup bound, Cauchy--Schwarz on the Lebesgue integral and \eqref{eq:bdg} with $p=2$,
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\sup_{r\le t}\|\mathcal P_y(\gamma)_r-\mathcal P_y(\tilde\gamma)_r\|_1^2\le\widetilde K^2\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\sup_{u\le s}\|\gamma_u-\tilde\gamma_u\|_1^2\,ds,
		\]
		with $\widetilde K^2=2e^{2cT}K^2(T+C_2)$, $K=4\max(\|A\|_\infty,\|L\|_\infty)$. Multiplying by $e^{-\beta t}$ and using $\sup_{t\le T}e^{-\beta t}\int_0^te^{\beta s}ds\le\beta^{-1}$ makes $\mathcal P_y$ a strict contraction for $\beta>\widetilde K^2$, and the Banach fixed point theorem applies.
		
		\emph{State space.} Once the solution, hence the deterministic path $\eta$, is fixed, \eqref{eq:mild} is a one-particle Belavkin equation with the bounded time-dependent self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t)$, and invariance of $\mathcal S$ is inherited from \cite[Thm.\ 2.8, 2.9]{Kolokoltsov2026}. The mean-field drift is of commutator form with a self-adjoint effective Hamiltonian, so it introduces no positivity- or trace-breaking mechanism.
		
		\emph{Purity.} With $\eta$ fixed, \eqref{eq:mild} is the one-particle case of Proposition \ref{prop:purity-N}, which gives the vector form \eqref{eq:reference-vector} and hence purity.
		
		\emph{Lipschitz dependence.} Apply the same bounds to $\mathcal P_y(\gamma^y)-\mathcal P_x(\gamma^x)=S_t(y-x)+[\text{difference of the nonlinear terms}]$ and use $(a+b+c)^2\le3(a^2+b^2+c^2)$ and Gr\"onwall's lemma.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:linear-flow}
		Fix the deterministic path $\eta$ of Lemma \ref{lem:reference} and let $\gamma_\cdot$ be the $B_1$-driven solution of \eqref{eq:mild}. For $h\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$ and a continuous adapted forcing $\Phi$ with $\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\|\Phi_t\|_1^2<\infty$, the linear mild equation
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:mild-linear}
			\xi_t=S_th-i\int_0^tS_{t-s}\big[\mathsf{B}(\eta_s),\xi_s\big]ds+\int_0^tS_{t-s}\Phi_s\,ds+\int_0^tS_{t-s}D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_s](\xi_s)\,dB_1(s)
		\end{equation}
		has a unique solution in $\mathcal C_{ad}([0,T];M_d(\mathbb{C}))$, depending linearly and continuously on $(h,\Phi)$, and there is $C_L=C_L(T,\|H\|_\infty,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty)$ with
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:linear-bound}
			\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\|\xi_t\|_1^4\le C_L\Big(\|h\|_1^4+\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\|\Phi_t\|_1^4\Big).
		\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:DM} and Lemmas \ref{lem:commutator}--\ref{lem:partial-trace}, $\|[\mathsf{B}(\eta_s),\xi]\|_1\le2\|A\|_\infty\|\xi\|_1$ and $\|D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_s](\xi)\|_1\le4\|L\|_\infty\|\xi\|_1$, using $\|\gamma_s\|_1=1$ and $|\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\gamma_s)|\le2\|L\|_\infty$. These bounds are uniform in $\omega$ and $s$, so \eqref{eq:mild-linear} is a linear mild equation with bounded coefficients; the contraction argument of Theorem \ref{thm:wellposed}, with $K$ replaced by $4\max(\|A\|_\infty,\|L\|_\infty)$, gives existence, uniqueness and linearity. For \eqref{eq:linear-bound}, apply \eqref{eq:bdg} with $p=4$ to the stochastic convolution, Cauchy--Schwarz to the Lebesgue terms, and Gr\"onwall's lemma.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:propagator}
		For $0\le s\le t\le T$ let $U^{t,s}h:=\xi_t$, where $\xi$ solves \eqref{eq:mild-linear} on $[s,t]$ with $\Phi\equiv0$ and $\xi_s=h$. Then $U^{t,s}$ is almost surely a bounded linear operator on $M_d(\mathbb{C})$ with $\sup_{0\le s\le t\le T}\mathbb{E}\|U^{t,s}\|^4\le C_L'$, $U^{t,t}=\mathrm{Id}$, and $U^{t,s}=U^{t,r}U^{r,s}$ for $s\le r\le t$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The moment bound follows from \eqref{eq:linear-bound} applied to a fixed basis $e_1,\dots,e_{d^2}$ of $M_d(\mathbb{C})$ with $\|e_i\|_1=1$: there is $c(d)$ with $\|U^{t,s}\|\le c(d)\max_i\|U^{t,s}e_i\|_1$, whence $\mathbb{E}\|U^{t,s}\|^4\le c(d)^4d^2C_L$. The cocycle property holds because $U^{t,r}U^{r,s}h$ and $U^{t,s}h$ solve the same linear equation on $[r,t]$ with the same value at $r$, and the coefficients depend only on the already-fixed $\gamma_\cdot$ and $\eta_\cdot$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:frechet}
		Fix $\eta$ as above and let $\gamma^y$ denote the solution of \eqref{eq:mild} with the mean-field path frozen at $\eta$ and initial datum $y$. The map $y\mapsto\gamma^y_\cdot$, from $\mathcal S$ into $\mathcal C_{ad}([0,T];M_d(\mathbb{C}))$, is Fr\'echet differentiable at every $y\in\mathcal S$, with derivative $h\mapsto U^{\cdot,0}h$, and with $R^h_t:=\gamma^{y+h}_t-\gamma^y_t-U^{t,0}h$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:frechet-quant}
			\Big(\mathbb{E}\sup_{t\le T}\|R^h_t\|_1^2\Big)^{1/2}\le \widetilde K_T^{1/2}\|h\|_1^2 .
		\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
With $\eta$ frozen the drift of \eqref{eq:mild} is linear in $\gamma$, so the only second-order remainder comes from $\mathcal{M}$. Writing $\delta_s=\gamma^{y+h}_s-\gamma^y_s$, the algebraic identity
		\[
		\mathcal{M}[\gamma+\delta]-\mathcal{M}[\gamma]=D\mathcal{M}[\gamma](\delta)-\operatorname{Tr}\big((L+L^\ast)\delta\big)\delta
		\]
		holds with no further terms, since $\mathcal{M}$ is the sum of a linear and a quadratic term. Subtracting the equation for $U^{\cdot,0}h$ therefore gives for $R^h$ the equation \eqref{eq:mild-linear} with $h=0$ and diffusion forcing $-\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\delta_s)\delta_s$, whose trace norm is at most $2\|L\|_\infty\|\delta_s\|_1^2$. Applying \eqref{eq:bdg} with $p=2$, Gr\"onwall's lemma, and the fourth-power version of \eqref{eq:lipschitz} (the same argument run with $p=4$, which \eqref{eq:bdg} permits), giving $\mathbb{E}\sup_{s\le T}\|\delta_s\|_1^4\le K_T\|h\|_1^4$, yields \eqref{eq:frechet-quant}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:adjoint}
		For $A_0\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal S$ set
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:adjoint}
			\mathcal{M}^\ast[A_0](\gamma):=A_0L+L^\ast A_0-\operatorname{Tr}\big((L+L^\ast)\gamma\big)A_0-\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\gamma)(L+L^\ast).
		\end{equation}
		Then $\operatorname{Tr}\big(A_0\,D\mathcal{M}[\gamma](\xi)\big)=\operatorname{Tr}\big(\mathcal{M}^\ast[A_0](\gamma)\,\xi\big)$ for all $\xi\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Expand $\operatorname{Tr}(A_0D\mathcal{M}[\gamma](\xi))$ into four terms using \eqref{eq:DM}. The first two give $\operatorname{Tr}((A_0L+L^\ast A_0)\xi)$ by cyclicity. In the third, $\xi$ enters through the scalar $\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\xi)$ multiplying the fixed operator $\gamma$; paired against $A_0$ it contributes the scalar $\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\gamma)$ multiplying the operator $L+L^\ast$, which is built from $L$ and not from $A_0$. The fourth is $\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\gamma)\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\xi)$. Collecting gives \eqref{eq:adjoint}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:adjoint-scope}
		Lemma \ref{lem:adjoint} is the duality used to test the linearised equation against observables. It does not determine the covariance of the idiosyncratic noise $V$ of \eqref{eq:intro-sys-3}: that covariance is a second-order object, identified in Theorem \ref{thm:covariance} as a limit of rescaled pair correlations. A closed form built from \eqref{eq:adjoint} alone would presume that the whole martingale part of $F^N$ is carried by coefficients that are functions of the one-particle state, which Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients} shows to be false.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:purity-N}
		Let $\Gamma^N_0=|\Psi_0\rangle\langle\Psi_0|$ with $\Psi_0\in\mathscr{H}^{\otimes N}$, $\|\Psi_0\|=1$. The equation
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:vector-N}
			d\Psi_t=\Big(-iH_N-\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^N\big(L_j^\ast L_j-\mu^{(j)}_tL_j+\tfrac14(\mu^{(j)}_t)^2\big)\Big)\Psi_t\,dt+\sum_{j=1}^N\Big(L_j-\tfrac{\mu^{(j)}_t}2\Big)\Psi_t\,dB_j(t),
		\end{equation}
		$\mu^{(j)}_t:=\langle\Psi_t,(L_j+L_j^\ast)\Psi_t\rangle$, has a unique global strong solution; $\|\Psi_t\|=1$ for all $t$ almost surely; and $\Gamma^N_t=|\Psi_t\rangle\langle\Psi_t|$ solves \eqref{eq:N-particle}. In particular $\Gamma^N_t$ is a rank-one projection for every $t$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The coefficients of \eqref{eq:vector-N} are polynomial in $(\Psi,\overline\Psi)$, hence locally Lipschitz, and a unique local solution exists up to the exit time from balls. Write $n_t:=\|\Psi_t\|^2$ and, for each $j$, $a_j:=-\tfrac12(L_j^\ast L_j-\mu^{(j)}L_j+\tfrac14(\mu^{(j)})^2)$, $b_j:=L_j-\tfrac{\mu^{(j)}}2$. Collecting the contributions $-\langle L^\ast_jL_j\rangle+\tfrac12(\mu^{(j)})^2-\tfrac14(\mu^{(j)})^2n$ from the drift and $\langle L^\ast_jL_j\rangle-\tfrac12(\mu^{(j)})^2+\tfrac14(\mu^{(j)})^2n$ from the It\^o correction, the drift of $n_t$ vanishes identically and the martingale part is $\sum_j\mu^{(j)}_t(1-n_t)dB_j(t)$. Hence
		\[
		d(1-n_t)=-(1-n_t)\sum_j\mu^{(j)}_t\,dB_j(t),
		\]
		so on each localising interval $1-n_t$ is a stochastic exponential started at $0$ and vanishes identically. Therefore $\|\Psi_t\|=1$, the coefficients are bounded along the solution, and the solution is global.
		
		Set $\widetilde\Gamma_t=|\Psi_t\rangle\langle\Psi_t|$. The It\^o product rule gives
		\[
		d\widetilde\Gamma_t=\Big(|a\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|+|\Psi\rangle\langle a\Psi|+\sum_j|b_j\Psi\rangle\langle b_j\Psi|\Big)dt+\sum_j\big(|b_j\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|+|\Psi\rangle\langle b_j\Psi|\big)dB_j,
		\]
		with $a$ the full drift operator. The coefficient of $dB_j$ is $L_j\widetilde\Gamma+\widetilde\Gamma L_j^\ast-\mu^{(j)}\widetilde\Gamma$, which is the coefficient in \eqref{eq:N-particle} because $\mu^{(j)}=\operatorname{Tr}((L_j+L_j^\ast)\widetilde\Gamma)$. In the drift, the terms proportional to $\mu^{(j)}(L_j\widetilde\Gamma+\widetilde\Gamma L_j^\ast)$ carry $+\tfrac12$ from $a$ and $-\tfrac12$ from $\sum_j|b_j\Psi\rangle\langle b_j\Psi|$ and cancel; those proportional to $(\mu^{(j)})^2\widetilde\Gamma$ carry $-\tfrac14$ and $+\tfrac14$ and cancel; what remains is $-i[H_N,\widetilde\Gamma]+\sum_j\mathcal{D}_j\widetilde\Gamma$. Pathwise uniqueness for \eqref{eq:N-particle} identifies $\Gamma^N_t=\widetilde\Gamma_t$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:A0-product}
		If $A=0$ then $\mathsf{B}\equiv0$ and, by the argument of Proposition \ref{prop:refutation}, $\Gamma^N_t=\bigotimes_j\gamma_{j,t}$ pathwise, that is $\Psi_t=\bigotimes_j\phi_{j,t}$ up to a phase. Every quantity introduced below vanishes identically in this case. Since the reference filters are attached to the labels and the labels are permuted together with the noises, the exchangeability in law of Section \ref{ssec:exch} extends: the joint law of $(\Psi_\cdot,(\phi_{j,\cdot})_{j\le N})$ is invariant under a simultaneous permutation of labels, so the law of any functional built from $\Psi$ and from $(\phi_i)_{i\in T}$ depends on $T$ only through $|T|$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:tau}
		For all $u,v\in\mathscr{H}^{\otimes N}$ and $S'\subseteq S$:
		(i) $\|\tau_S(u,v)\|_1\le\|u\|\|v\|$;
		(ii) $\operatorname{Tr}_{S'}\tau_S(u,v)=\tau_{S\setminus S'}(u,v)$;
		(iii) if $k\in S$ and $p_ku=u$, $p_kv=v$, then $\tau_S(u,v)=\tau_{S\setminus\{k\}}(u,v)\otimes p_k$, the second factor in slot $k$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
(i) $\||u\rangle\langle v|\|_1=\|u\|\|v\|$ and a partial trace is a contraction for the trace norm. (ii) is the tower property. (iii) $p_ku=u$ means $u=\phi_k\otimes u'$ after moving slot $k$ to the front, and likewise for $v$; then $|u\rangle\langle v|=p_k\otimes|u'\rangle\langle v'|$, and the partial trace over $S^c$ does not touch slot $k\in S$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:dict-two}
		Pathwise, for every $t$, every $N\ge2$ and all distinct labels $i,j$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:dict-1}
			\big\|\Gamma^{(i)}_t-\gamma_{i,t}\big\|_1\le 4\varepsilon_i,
		\end{equation}
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:dict-2}
			\big\|\Delta^{(ij)}_t\big\|_1\le 64\big(\varepsilon_{ij}+\varepsilon_i^2+\varepsilon_j^2\big).
		\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Take $i=1$, $j=2$; the statement is pathwise and algebraic. Throughout $\gamma_1=p_1$, $\gamma_2=p_2$ as operators on the respective slots.
		
		\emph{Proof of \eqref{eq:dict-1}.} With $S=\{1\}$, \eqref{eq:expansion} reads $\Gamma^{(1)}=\tau_1(p_1\Psi,p_1\Psi)+\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,p_1\Psi)+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)$, and by Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(iii) the first term is $\|p_1\Psi\|^2p_1=(1-\varepsilon_1^2)p_1$. With $X_1:=\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)$,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}-p_1=-\varepsilon_1^2p_1+X_1+X_1^\ast+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi),
		\]
		so $\|\Gamma^{(1)}-p_1\|_1\le2\varepsilon_1^2+2\varepsilon_1\le4\varepsilon_1$ by Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(i).
		
		\emph{Proof of \eqref{eq:dict-2}.} Let $S=\{1,2\}$ and write $\Psi_{pp}:=\Psi^S_\emptyset$, $\Psi_{qp}:=\Psi^S_{\{1\}}$, $\Psi_{pq}:=\Psi^S_{\{2\}}$, $\Psi_{qq}:=\Psi^S_{\{1,2\}}$, so $\|\Psi_{qp}\|\le\varepsilon_1$, $\|\Psi_{pq}\|\le\varepsilon_2$, $\|\Psi_{qq}\|=\varepsilon_{12}$, $\|\Psi_{pp}\|\le1$ and
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:norm-split}
			1-\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2=\|\Psi_{qp}\|^2+\|\Psi_{pq}\|^2+\|\Psi_{qq}\|^2\le2(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2).
		\end{equation}
		Set $X:=\tau_1(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{qp})$ and $Y:=\tau_2(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pq})$, with $\|X\|_1\le\varepsilon_1$, $\|Y\|_1\le\varepsilon_2$. By \eqref{eq:factorisation} with $U=\emptyset,\{1\},\{2\}$ and Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(ii),
		\[
		\tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pp})=\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2p_1\otimes p_2,\qquad \tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{qp})=X\otimes p_2,\qquad \tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pq})=p_1\otimes Y,
		\]
		so
		\[
		\Gamma^{(12)}=\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2p_1\otimes p_2+\big(X\otimes p_2+\mathrm{h.c.}\big)+\big(p_1\otimes Y+\mathrm{h.c.}\big)+R,
		\]
		where $R$ collects the remaining nine terms of \eqref{eq:expansion}, namely those in which at least one of $T,T'$ equals $\{1,2\}$, or $\{T,T'\}$ is one of $\{\{1\},\{2\}\}$, $\{\{1\},\{1\}\}$, $\{\{2\},\{2\}\}$. By \eqref{eq:expansion} and $\varepsilon_{12}\le\min(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\le1$,
		\[
		\|R\|_1\le2\varepsilon_{12}+2(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2)\varepsilon_{12}+\varepsilon_{12}^2+2\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2\le2\varepsilon_{12}+8(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2).
		\]
		By Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(ii) and the same expansion for $S=\{1\}$,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}=p_1+X+X^\ast+E_1,\qquad E_1:=-\varepsilon_1^2p_1+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)+\big(\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)-X\big)+\mathrm{h.c.},
		\]
		and $\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)-X=\tau_1(\Psi_{pq},\Psi_{qp})+\tau_1(\Psi_{pp}+\Psi_{pq},\Psi_{qq})$, whence
		\[
		\|E_1\|_1\le2\varepsilon_1^2+2\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2+4\varepsilon_{12}\le4\varepsilon_{12}+3(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2),
		\]
		and symmetrically $\Gamma^{(2)}=p_2+Y+Y^\ast+E_2$ with the same bound. Multiplying out,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}=p_1\otimes p_2+(X+X^\ast)\otimes p_2+p_1\otimes(Y+Y^\ast)+E_1\otimes p_2+p_1\otimes E_2+\rho,
		\]
		where $\rho$ collects all products of two nonleading factors, so that $\|\rho\|_1\le(2\varepsilon_1+\|E_1\|_1)(2\varepsilon_2+\|E_2\|_1)\le27(\varepsilon_{12}+\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2)$. Subtracting and using \eqref{eq:norm-split}, every term of order $\varepsilon_1$ or $\varepsilon_2$ alone cancels and
		\[
		\Delta^{(12)}=\big(\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2-1\big)p_1\otimes p_2+R-E_1\otimes p_2-p_1\otimes E_2-\rho,
		\]
		which gives \eqref{eq:dict-2} after collecting constants.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
With $S=\{1\}$, \eqref{eq:expansion} reads $\Gamma^{(1)}=\tau_1(p_1\Psi,p_1\Psi)+\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,p_1\Psi)+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)$, and by Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(iii) the first term is $\|p_1\Psi\|^2p_1=(1-\varepsilon_1^2)p_1$. With $X_1:=\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)$,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}-p_1=-\varepsilon_1^2p_1+X_1+X_1^\ast+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi),
		\]
		so $\|\Gamma^{(1)}-p_1\|_1\le2\varepsilon_1^2+2\varepsilon_1\le4\varepsilon_1$ by Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(i).
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
Let $S=\{1,2\}$ and write $\Psi_{pp}:=\Psi^S_\emptyset$, $\Psi_{qp}:=\Psi^S_{\{1\}}$, $\Psi_{pq}:=\Psi^S_{\{2\}}$, $\Psi_{qq}:=\Psi^S_{\{1,2\}}$, so $\|\Psi_{qp}\|\le\varepsilon_1$, $\|\Psi_{pq}\|\le\varepsilon_2$, $\|\Psi_{qq}\|=\varepsilon_{12}$, $\|\Psi_{pp}\|\le1$ and
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:norm-split}
			1-\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2=\|\Psi_{qp}\|^2+\|\Psi_{pq}\|^2+\|\Psi_{qq}\|^2\le2(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2).
		\end{equation}
		Set $X:=\tau_1(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{qp})$ and $Y:=\tau_2(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pq})$, with $\|X\|_1\le\varepsilon_1$, $\|Y\|_1\le\varepsilon_2$. By \eqref{eq:factorisation} with $U=\emptyset,\{1\},\{2\}$ and Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(ii),
		\[
		\tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pp})=\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2p_1\otimes p_2,\qquad \tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{qp})=X\otimes p_2,\qquad \tau_S(\Psi_{pp},\Psi_{pq})=p_1\otimes Y,
		\]
		so
		\[
		\Gamma^{(12)}=\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2p_1\otimes p_2+\big(X\otimes p_2+\mathrm{h.c.}\big)+\big(p_1\otimes Y+\mathrm{h.c.}\big)+R,
		\]
		where $R$ collects the remaining nine terms of \eqref{eq:expansion}, namely those in which at least one of $T,T'$ equals $\{1,2\}$, or $\{T,T'\}$ is one of $\{\{1\},\{2\}\}$, $\{\{1\},\{1\}\}$, $\{\{2\},\{2\}\}$. By \eqref{eq:expansion} and $\varepsilon_{12}\le\min(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\le1$,
		\[
		\|R\|_1\le2\varepsilon_{12}+2(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2)\varepsilon_{12}+\varepsilon_{12}^2+2\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2\le2\varepsilon_{12}+8(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2).
		\]
		By Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(ii) and the same expansion for $S=\{1\}$,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}=p_1+X+X^\ast+E_1,\qquad E_1:=-\varepsilon_1^2p_1+\tau_1(q_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)+\big(\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)-X\big)+\mathrm{h.c.},
		\]
		and $\tau_1(p_1\Psi,q_1\Psi)-X=\tau_1(\Psi_{pq},\Psi_{qp})+\tau_1(\Psi_{pp}+\Psi_{pq},\Psi_{qq})$, whence
		\[
		\|E_1\|_1\le2\varepsilon_1^2+2\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2+4\varepsilon_{12}\le4\varepsilon_{12}+3(\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2),
		\]
		and symmetrically $\Gamma^{(2)}=p_2+Y+Y^\ast+E_2$ with the same bound. Multiplying out,
		\[
		\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}=p_1\otimes p_2+(X+X^\ast)\otimes p_2+p_1\otimes(Y+Y^\ast)+E_1\otimes p_2+p_1\otimes E_2+\rho,
		\]
		where $\rho$ collects all products of two nonleading factors, so that $\|\rho\|_1\le(2\varepsilon_1+\|E_1\|_1)(2\varepsilon_2+\|E_2\|_1)\le27(\varepsilon_{12}+\varepsilon_1^2+\varepsilon_2^2)$. Subtracting and using \eqref{eq:norm-split}, every term of order $\varepsilon_1$ or $\varepsilon_2$ alone cancels and
		\[
		\Delta^{(12)}=\big(\|\Psi_{pp}\|^2-1\big)p_1\otimes p_2+R-E_1\otimes p_2-p_1\otimes E_2-\rho,
		\]
		which gives \eqref{eq:dict-2} after collecting constants.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:cancellation}
		The content of \eqref{eq:dict-2} is the cancellation. Individually, $\Gamma^{(12)}$ and $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$ differ from $p_1\otimes p_2$ by terms of size $\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\asymp N^{-1/2}$; only in the difference do these cancel, leaving the order $N^{-1}$. The mechanism is \eqref{eq:factorisation}: every term of total degree $|U|<|S|$ is a product across a nontrivial partition of $S$ and is reproduced by the corresponding term of $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:dict-three}
		There is an absolute constant $c_3$ such that, pathwise, for all distinct labels $i,j,k$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:dict-3}
			\big\|\Delta^{(ijk)}_t\big\|_1\le c_3\big(\varepsilon_{ijk}+\varepsilon_{ij}\varepsilon_k+\varepsilon_{ik}\varepsilon_j+\varepsilon_{jk}\varepsilon_i+\varepsilon_i^2\varepsilon_j^2+\varepsilon_i^2\varepsilon_k^2+\varepsilon_j^2\varepsilon_k^2\big).
		\end{equation}
		More generally, for $S$ with $|S|=m$, $\|\Delta^{(S)}\|_1\le c_m\sum\varepsilon_T\varepsilon_{T'}$, the sum running over pairs $T,T'\subseteq S$ with $|T\cup T'|=m$, together with the products of two such factors arising from the lower marginals.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Take $S=\{1,2,3\}$ and insert the expansion \eqref{eq:expansion} for $\Gamma^{(S)}$ and for each marginal $\Gamma^{(S')}$, $S'\subsetneq S$, into \eqref{eq:cumulant3}. By \eqref{eq:factorisation}, every term of \eqref{eq:expansion} indexed by $(T,T')$ with $U=T\cup T'\subsetneq S$ is a tensor product of $\tau_U(\Psi^S_T,\Psi^S_{T'})$ with the projections $p_i$, $i\in S\setminus U$; and by Lemma \ref{lem:tau}(ii) the factor $\tau_U(\Psi^S_T,\Psi^S_{T'})$ is the term indexed by $(T,T')$ in the expansion of $\Gamma^{(U)}$. Since \eqref{eq:cumulant3} is the alternating sum which annihilates every operator factorising across a nontrivial partition of $S$ with each block factor equal to the corresponding marginal, all such terms cancel, with the exception of the cross terms produced when a marginal is replaced by its own expansion; each such cross term is a product of at least two factors $\tau_{U'}(\Psi_T,\Psi_{T'})$ with $U'\ne\emptyset$ and disjoint index sets, hence is bounded by a product of at least two amplitudes. The surviving terms are those with $|T\cup T'|=3$, bounded by $\varepsilon_{123}+\varepsilon_{ij}\varepsilon_k$ over all assignments, together with the cross terms, bounded by $\varepsilon_i^2\varepsilon_j^2$ and its permutations, up to a combinatorial constant. The general statement follows by the same argument, the only change being the number of terms.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:orders}
		With the expected orders $\varepsilon_i\asymp N^{-1/2}$, $\varepsilon_{ij}\asymp N^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_{ijk}\asymp N^{-3/2}$, the right sides of \eqref{eq:dict-1}, \eqref{eq:dict-2}, \eqref{eq:dict-3} are of order $N^{-1/2}$, $N^{-1}$, $N^{-3/2}$: the mean-field orders of $\|\Gamma^{(1)}-\gamma\|_1$, $\|\Delta^{(12)}\|_1$ and $\|\Delta^{(123)}\|_1$.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:coefficients}
		For every $N\ge2$, every $t\ge0$ and every sample path,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:C1}
			C_1(t)=\mathcal{M}\big[\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big],
		\end{equation}
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:Cj}
			C_j(t)=\Theta^{(1j)}_t:=\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[(1\otimes L)\Delta^{(1j)}_t\big]+\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[\Delta^{(1j)}_t(1\otimes L^\ast)\big],\qquad j\ge2 .
		\end{equation}
		In particular $\|\Theta^{(1j)}_t\|_1\le2\|L\|_\infty\|\Delta^{(1j)}_t\|_1$. Moreover, for $A_0\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-test}
			\operatorname{Tr}\big(A_0\Theta^{(1j)}_t\big)=\operatorname{Tr}\Big[\big(A_0\otimes(L+L^\ast)\big)\Delta^{(1j)}_t\Big].
		\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
By (PT3), the scalar in \eqref{eq:reduced-sde} is $\operatorname{Tr}((L_j+L_j^\ast)\Gamma^N_t)=\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\Gamma^{(j)}_t)=m^{(j)}_t$ for every $j$; this is a partial-trace identity, not a symmetry statement. For $j=1$, (PT1) gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{2,\dots,N}(L_1\Gamma^N_t)=L\Gamma^{(1)}_t$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{2,\dots,N}(\Gamma^N_tL_1^\ast)=\Gamma^{(1)}_tL^\ast$, whence \eqref{eq:C1}, since $m^{(1)}_t=\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)\Gamma^{(1)}_t)$.
		
		For $j\ge2$, (PT3) gives
		\[
		C_j(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[(1\otimes L)\Gamma^{(1,j)}_t\big]+\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[\Gamma^{(1,j)}_t(1\otimes L^\ast)\big]-m^{(j)}_t\Gamma^{(1)}_t .
		\]
		Insert $\Gamma^{(1,j)}_t=\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t+\Delta^{(1j)}_t$. By (PT1)--(PT2),
		\[
		\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[(1\otimes L)(\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t)\big]=\operatorname{Tr}\big(L\Gamma^{(j)}_t\big)\Gamma^{(1)}_t,\qquad
		\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[(\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t)(1\otimes L^\ast)\big]=\operatorname{Tr}\big(L^\ast\Gamma^{(j)}_t\big)\Gamma^{(1)}_t,
		\]
		and the sum of the two scalars is $m^{(j)}_t$. The factorised contribution therefore cancels the subtraction, leaving \eqref{eq:Cj}. The norm bound is Lemma \ref{lem:partial-trace} applied to each partial trace. Identity \eqref{eq:theta-test} follows from $\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\operatorname{Tr}_2X)=\operatorname{Tr}((A_0\otimes1)X)$ together with $(A_0\otimes1)(1\otimes L)=A_0\otimes L$ and $(1\otimes L^\ast)(A_0\otimes1)=A_0\otimes L^\ast$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:coefficient-correction}
		The scalar subtracted in \eqref{eq:reduced-sde} cancels against the factorised part of $\Gamma^{(1,j)}$ with the mean $m^{(j)}$ of particle $j$ itself, not with $m^{(1)}$. Replacing $m^{(j)}$ by $m^{(1)}$ and $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}$ by $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(1)}$ is valid only under pathwise permutation symmetry, and the resulting object fails at $A=0$: it does not vanish while the left side does. With the connected correlation of the actual pair the identity holds with no error term and no symmetry hypothesis, and there is one coefficient $\Theta^{(1j)}$ for each $j$, not a single $j$-independent operator.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:pair}
		Pathwise, for every $N\ge3$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:pair-sde}
			d\mathsf D_t=\Phi_t\,dt+\sum_{j=1}^NG_j(t)\,dB_j(t),
		\end{equation}
		with
		\begin{align}
			G_1&=(L\otimes1)\mathsf D+\mathsf D(L^\ast\otimes1)-m^{(1)}_t\mathsf D-\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Theta^{(21)}_t,&&\|G_1\|_1\le6\|L\|_\infty\|\mathsf D\|_1,\label{eq:G1}\\
			G_2&=(1\otimes L)\mathsf D+\mathsf D(1\otimes L^\ast)-m^{(2)}_t\mathsf D-\Theta^{(12)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}_t,&&\|G_2\|_1\le6\|L\|_\infty\|\mathsf D\|_1,\label{eq:G2}\\
			G_j&=\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[(1\otimes1\otimes L)\Delta^{(12j)}_t\big]+\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[\Delta^{(12j)}_t(1\otimes1\otimes L^\ast)\big],&&\|G_j\|_1\le2\|L\|_\infty\|\Delta^{(12j)}_t\|_1,\ j\ge3,\label{eq:Gj}
		\end{align}
		and drift
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:pair-drift}
			\Phi_t=-i\big[H\otimes1+1\otimes H,\mathsf D_t\big]+(\mathcal{D}_1+\mathcal{D}_2)\mathsf D_t+S(t)+\sum_{j\ge3}R_j(t)-I(t),
		\end{equation}
		where $\mathcal{D}_1,\mathcal{D}_2$ are the one-particle dissipators on the respective slots,
		\[
		S(t):=-\tfrac iN\big[A,\Gamma^{(1,2)}_t\big]+\tfrac iN\big(\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\Gamma^{(1,2)}_t]\big)\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}_t+\tfrac iN\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\big(\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\widehat\Gamma^{(2,1)}_t]\big),\qquad \|S(t)\|_1\le\tfrac{6\|A\|_\infty}N,
		\]
		with $\widehat\Gamma^{(2,1)}$ the $(2,1)$-marginal arranged with particle $2$ first,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:Rj}
			\begin{split}
				R_j(t):=-\tfrac iN\Big(&\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[\widetilde A_{13},\,\mathsf D_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t+\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Delta^{(2j)}_t+\Delta^{(12j)}_t\big]\\
				&+\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[\widetilde A_{23},\,\mathsf D_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t+[\Delta^{(1j)}_t]_{13}\otimes[\Gamma^{(2)}_t]_2+\Delta^{(12j)}_t\big]\Big),
			\end{split}
		\end{equation}
		so that $\|R_j(t)\|_1\le\tfrac{2\|A\|_\infty}N(2\|\mathsf D_t\|_1+\|\Delta^{(1j)}_t\|_1+\|\Delta^{(2j)}_t\|_1+2\|\Delta^{(12j)}_t\|_1)$, and the It\^o correction
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ito-correction}
			I(t):=\sum_{j=1}^NC_j(t)\otimes C'_j(t)=\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(1)}_t]\otimes\Theta^{(21)}_t+\Theta^{(12)}_t\otimes\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(2)}_t]+\sum_{j\ge3}\Theta^{(1j)}_t\otimes\Theta^{(2j)}_t,
		\end{equation}
		$C'_j(t)$ being the martingale coefficients of $\Gamma^{(2)}_t$; thus
		\[
		\|I(t)\|_1\le16\|L\|_\infty^2\|\mathsf D_t\|_1+4\|L\|_\infty^2\sum_{j\ge3}\|\Delta^{(1j)}_t\|_1\|\Delta^{(2j)}_t\|_1 .
		\]
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
\emph{Coefficients of $d\Gamma^{(1,2)}_t$.} Trace \eqref{eq:N-particle} over particles $3,\dots,N$ and use (PT1)--(PT3): the coefficient of $dB_1$ is $(L\otimes1)\Gamma^{(1,2)}+\Gamma^{(1,2)}(L^\ast\otimes1)-m^{(1)}\Gamma^{(1,2)}$, symmetrically for $dB_2$; for $j\ge3$ the computation of Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients}, applied to the pair marginal, gives
		\[
		\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[(1\otimes1\otimes L)\Xi^{(j)}_t\big]+\operatorname{Tr}_3\big[\Xi^{(j)}_t(1\otimes1\otimes L^\ast)\big],\qquad \Xi^{(j)}_t:=\Gamma^{(1,2,j)}_t-\Gamma^{(1,2)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}_t,
		\]
		the factorised part again cancelling $m^{(j)}\Gamma^{(1,2)}$. The drift of $\Gamma^{(1,2)}$ is
		\[
		-i[H\otimes1+1\otimes H,\Gamma^{(1,2)}]+(\mathcal{D}_1+\mathcal{D}_2)\Gamma^{(1,2)}-\tfrac iN[A,\Gamma^{(1,2)}]-\tfrac iN\sum_{j\ge3}\big(\operatorname{Tr}_3[\widetilde A_{13},\Gamma^{(1,2,j)}]+\operatorname{Tr}_3[\widetilde A_{23},\Gamma^{(1,2,j)}]\big),
		\]
		by cyclicity (PT2) for the traced Hamiltonian, dissipator and interaction terms, each $j$ kept separate.
		
		\emph{Coefficients of $d(\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}_t)$.} The It\^o product rule with the coefficients of Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients} for both marginals gives drift $\mathcal{L}^{(1)}_N\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}+\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{(2)}_N+\sum_jC_j\otimes C'_j$ and, for each $j$, martingale coefficient $C_j\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}+\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes C'_j$; cross-variations of distinct $B_j$ vanish, and matching indices produce \eqref{eq:ito-correction}, with $C_1=\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(1)}]$, $C'_2=\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(2)}]$, $C_j=\Theta^{(1j)}$ for $j\ge2$ and $C'_j=\Theta^{(2j)}$ for $j\ne2$.
		
		\emph{Martingale coefficients of $\mathsf D$.} For $j=1$: substituting $\Gamma^{(1,2)}=\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}+\mathsf D$ into the $dB_1$ coefficient, the factorised part reassembles to $\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(1)}]\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$, which cancels $C_1\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$, leaving \eqref{eq:G1}; symmetrically \eqref{eq:G2}. For $j\ge3$, decompose by \eqref{eq:cumulant3},
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:xi-decomp}
			\Xi^{(j)}_t=[\Delta^{(1j)}_t]_{13}\otimes[\Gamma^{(2)}_t]_2+\Gamma^{(1)}_t\otimes\Delta^{(2j)}_t+\Delta^{(12j)}_t;
		\end{equation}
		by (PT1)--(PT3) the $\Delta^{(1j)}$ piece contributes $\Theta^{(1j)}\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$, cancelling $C_j\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$, the $\Delta^{(2j)}$ piece contributes $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Theta^{(2j)}$, cancelling $\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes C'_j$, and the irreducible piece survives, giving \eqref{eq:Gj}.
		
		\emph{Drift of $\mathsf D$.} The local Hamiltonian and dissipator terms subtract to their action on $\mathsf D$, since $[H\otimes1,X\otimes Y]=[H,X]\otimes Y$ and $\mathcal{D}_1(X\otimes Y)=(\mathcal{D} X)\otimes Y$. Among the interaction terms, the pieces with an explicit prefactor $1/N$ acting on pair marginals are collected in $S(t)$. For each $j\ge3$, subtract the term $(\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\Gamma^{(1,j)}])\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$ of $\mathcal{L}^{(1)}_N\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$ from $\operatorname{Tr}_3[\widetilde A_{13},\Gamma^{(1,2,j)}]$: decomposing $\Gamma^{(1,2,j)}$ by \eqref{eq:cumulant3} and $\Gamma^{(1,j)}=\Gamma^{(1)}\otimes\Gamma^{(j)}+\Delta^{(1j)}$, the fully factorised parts cancel through (PT4), both being $[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{(j)}),\Gamma^{(1)}]\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$, and the $\Delta^{(1j)}$ parts cancel through (PT3), both being $(\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\Delta^{(1j)}])\otimes\Gamma^{(2)}$; the surviving pieces are the first line of \eqref{eq:Rj}. The $\widetilde A_{23}$ terms are treated symmetrically against the particle-$2$ sum. Subtracting \eqref{eq:ito-correction} gives \eqref{eq:pair-drift}. The bound on $I(t)$ uses $\|\mathcal{M}[\rho]\|_1\le4\|L\|_\infty$ on $\mathcal S$ and Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:pair-structure}
		Two structural points. The quadratic-variation contributions do not cancel between the two sides: they survive as $I(t)$, which contains $N-2$ products of pair-correlation coefficients. And the equation closes on the irreducible three-body cumulant only when it is posed for the connected correlation of distinct particles; \eqref{eq:xi-decomp} is where this enters. A first-moment hypothesis on the three-body cumulant does not suffice to run a Gr\"onwall argument on \eqref{eq:pair-sde}, because the It\^o sum couples $N-2$ products of pair coefficients, so the natural closure is at the level of second moments with fourth-moment input one level down. In the present development the rates of Section \ref{sec:amplitude-hyp} are obtained from the amplitude bounds instead, and \eqref{eq:pair-sde} is used only in Proposition \ref{prop:xi-compact}, for an equicontinuity bound.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:F-decomp}
		Pathwise,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:F-sde}
			\begin{split}
				dF^N_t=\Big(&-i\big[H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),F^N_t\big]+\mathcal{D} F^N_t-i\big[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]+r^{(1)}_N(t)\Big)dt\\
				&+\Big(D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_t](F^N_t)+r^{(2)}_N(t)\Big)dB_1(t)+\sqrt N\sum_{j\ge2}\Theta^{(1j)}_t\,dB_j(t),
			\end{split}
		\end{equation}
		with $F^N_0=0$ and
		\[
		r^{(1)}_N(t)=\tfrac i{\sqrt N}\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]-\tfrac i{\sqrt N}\sum_{j\ge2}\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[A,\Delta^{(1j)}_t\big]+\varrho^{\,\prime}_N(t),\qquad
		r^{(2)}_N(t)=-\tfrac1{\sqrt N}\operatorname{Tr}\big((L+L^\ast)F^N_t\big)F^N_t,
		\]
		where $\|\varrho^{\,\prime}_N(t)\|_1\le2\|A\|_\infty N^{-1/2}\|\widehat{G}^N_t\|_1$ accounts for the difference between $\overline\Gamma_t$ and $\Gamma^{\ne1}_t$, and
		\[
		\big\|r^{(2)}_N(t)\big\|_1\le\tfrac{2\|L\|_\infty}{\sqrt N}\|F^N_t\|_1^2\le4\|L\|_\infty\|F^N_t\|_1 .
		\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Subtract \eqref{eq:reference} for $j=1$ from \eqref{eq:reduced-sde} and multiply by $\sqrt N$. For the martingale part: the $dB_1$ coefficient is $\sqrt N(\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(1)}_t]-\mathcal{M}[\gamma_t])$ by \eqref{eq:C1}, and the algebraic expansion of $\mathcal{M}$ used in Theorem \ref{thm:frechet}, applied with $\delta=N^{-1/2}F^N_t$, gives $D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_t](F^N_t)+r^{(2)}_N(t)$; the $dB_j$ coefficients, $j\ge2$, are $\sqrt N\,\Theta^{(1j)}_t$ by \eqref{eq:Cj}. For the drift, use \eqref{eq:reduced-drift} and
		\[
		\sqrt N\Big(\tfrac{N-1}N\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]-\big[\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),\gamma_t\big]\Big)
		=\big[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]+\big[\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),F^N_t\big]-\tfrac1{\sqrt N}\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]+\varrho^{\,\prime}_N(t),
		\]
		by bilinearity of $(\rho,\sigma)\mapsto[\mathsf{B}(\rho),\sigma]$, where $\varrho^{\,\prime}_N$ collects $\sqrt N[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t-\overline\Gamma_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t]$ and $\|\Gamma^{\ne1}_t-\overline\Gamma_t\|_1\le2/N$ gives the stated bound after inserting $\overline\Gamma_t=\eta_t+N^{-1/2}\widehat{G}^N_t$. Collecting terms yields \eqref{eq:F-sde}. The bound on $r^{(2)}_N$ uses $\|F^N_t\|_1\le2\sqrt N$ pathwise.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:F-structure}
		The mean-field component of the noise is carried by $B_1$ with coefficient $D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_t](F^N_t)$ up to a remainder of order $N^{-1/2}$, and needs no decomposition into a conditional mean and a residual. The idiosyncratic component is $\sqrt N\sum_{j\ge2}\Theta^{(1j)}dB_j$, whose predictable bracket carries the normalisation of Proposition \ref{prop:qv}. The drift coupling $-i[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t]$ to the empirical fluctuation is of order one and cannot be removed; the limiting equation contains it, which is what makes the limit a system.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:G-decomp}
		Pathwise, for every $N\ge2$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:G-sde}
			d\widehat{G}^N_t=\Big(-i\big[H+\mathsf{B}(\eta_t),\widehat{G}^N_t\big]-i\big[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N_t),\eta_t\big]+\mathcal{D}\widehat{G}^N_t+\varrho_N(t)\Big)dt+dM^{\mathrm{mf}}_t,\qquad \widehat{G}^N_0=0,
		\end{equation}
		where
		\[
		M^{\mathrm{mf}}_t:=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^N\int_0^t\mathcal{M}\big[\Gamma^{(j)}_s\big]dB_j(s)+\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{k=1}^N\int_0^t\Big(\sum_{j\ne k}\Theta^{(jk)}_s\Big)dB_k(s),
		\]
		and
		\[
		\|\varrho_N(t)\|_1\le\frac1{\sqrt N}\Big(2\|A\|_\infty+c_A\|\widehat{G}^N_t\|_1^2\Big)+2\|A\|_\infty\sqrt N\cdot\frac1{N^2}\sum_{j\ne k}\big\|\Delta^{(jk)}_t\big\|_1,
		\]
		with $c_A=c(d)\|A\|_\infty$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Average \eqref{eq:reduced-sde}, in the form given for a general label $j$ by \eqref{eq:reduced-drift} and Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients}, over $j=1,\dots,N$. The martingale part is $M^{\mathrm{mf}}$ by inspection. In the drift, the local terms give $-i[H,\overline\Gamma]+\mathcal{D}\overline\Gamma$; for the mean-field terms use $\tfrac{N-1}N\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne j})=\mathsf{B}(\overline\Gamma)-\tfrac1N\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{(j)})$, whence
		\[
		\frac1N\sum_j\tfrac{N-1}N\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne j}),\Gamma^{(j)}\big]=\big[\mathsf{B}(\overline\Gamma),\overline\Gamma\big]-\frac1{N^2}\sum_j\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{(j)}),\Gamma^{(j)}\big],
		\]
		the last term bounded by $2\|A\|_\infty/N$ in trace norm. Subtract \eqref{eq:hartree}, multiply by $\sqrt N$, and expand using $\overline\Gamma=\eta+N^{-1/2}\widehat{G}^N$ and bilinearity:
		\[
		\sqrt N\Big(\big[\mathsf{B}(\overline\Gamma),\overline\Gamma\big]-\big[\mathsf{B}(\eta),\eta\big]\Big)=\big[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N),\eta\big]+\big[\mathsf{B}(\eta),\widehat{G}^N\big]+\frac1{\sqrt N}\big[\mathsf{B}(\widehat{G}^N),\widehat{G}^N\big].
		\]
		The pair-correlation terms contribute $\sqrt N\,N^{-2}\sum_j\sum_{k\ne j}\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\Delta^{(jk)}]$, bounded as stated by Lemma \ref{lem:partial-trace}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
\label{rem:G-autonomous}
		The drift of \eqref{eq:G-sde} involves neither the tagged fluctuation nor the tagged state: $\widehat{G}^N$ is autonomous up to the remainder. This is a consequence of the reference filters being independent and identically distributed, so that averages of functions of $\gamma_{j,s}$ over $j$ obey a law of large numbers with a deterministic limit. The field was invisible under the aggregate coupling refuted in Proposition \ref{prop:refutation}.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:deviation}
		Pathwise,
		\[
		\big\|\overline\Gamma_t-\eta_t\big\|_1\le\frac4N\sum_{j=1}^N\varepsilon_j(t)+\Big\|\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N\big(\gamma_{j,t}-\eta_t\big)\Big\|_1,
		\]
		and consequently, unconditionally,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:deviation}
			\mathbb{E}\big\|\widehat{G}^N_t\big\|_1^2\;=\;N\,\mathbb{E}\big\|\overline\Gamma_t-\eta_t\big\|_1^2\;\le\;32\,\mathbb{E}\big\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\big\rangle+8d .
		\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
The pathwise bound is the triangle inequality together with \eqref{eq:dict-1} applied termwise. For \eqref{eq:deviation}, use $(a+b)^2\le2a^2+2b^2$. By Cauchy--Schwarz, $\big(\tfrac4N\sum_j\varepsilon_j\big)^2\le\tfrac{16}N\sum_j\varepsilon_j^2=\tfrac{16}N\langle\Psi,\widehat{\mathcal N}\Psi\rangle$, so the first term contributes at most $32\,\mathbb{E}\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle$ after multiplication by $N$. For the second, $\|\cdot\|_1^2\le d\|\cdot\|_2^2$ and the $\gamma_{j,t}$ are independent and identically distributed with mean $\eta_t$ (Lemma \ref{lem:reference}), so
		\[
		N\,\mathbb{E}\Big\|\frac1N\sum_j(\gamma_{j,t}-\eta_t)\Big\|_2^2=\mathbb{E}\|\gamma_{1,t}-\eta_t\|_2^2\le4,
		\]
		contributing at most $8d$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:deviation}
		Lemma \ref{lem:deviation} is used twice: it supplies the moment bound for $\widehat{G}^N$ from a bound on the mean excitation number alone, with no decorrelation input (Corollary \ref{cor:G-moment}), and it is the quantitative half of the mechanism by which single excitations are created only through the deviation of the empirical mean field from $\eta$, which is the point at which the Gr\"onwall argument for the excitation number closes (Step 3 of the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:A1}).
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:orthogonality}
		For every self-adjoint $A_0\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$ and every $N$, $\big\langle B_1,\operatorname{Tr}(A_0M^{\mathrm{id}})\big\rangle_t\equiv0$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Immediate from the independence of $B_1$ and $B_j$, $j\ge2$: by Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients} the whole $B_1$-dependence of the martingale part of $F^N$ sits in the single coefficient $D\mathcal{M}[\gamma_t](F^N_t)+r^{(2)}_N(t)$, and $M^{\mathrm{id}}$ involves no $dB_1$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:qv}
		For self-adjoint $A_0,B_0\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qv}
			\big\langle\operatorname{Tr}(A_0M^{\mathrm{id}}),\operatorname{Tr}(B_0M^{\mathrm{id}})\big\rangle_t=\int_0^t\widehat\Sigma^N_s(A_0,B_0)\,ds,\qquad
			\widehat\Sigma^N_s(A_0,B_0):=N\sum_{j\ge2}\operatorname{Tr}\big(A_0\Theta^{(1j)}_s\big)\operatorname{Tr}\big(B_0\Theta^{(1j)}_s\big),
		\end{equation}
		and $|\operatorname{Tr}(A_0\Theta^{(1j)}_s)|\le2\|L\|_\infty\|A_0\|_\infty\|\Delta^{(1j)}_s\|_1$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
It\^o's isometry for the independent $B_j$, together with Proposition \ref{prop:coefficients}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:A1}
		Under Assumption \ref{assum:generators}, with $\Gamma^N_0=\gamma_0^{\otimes N}$, $\gamma_0=|\psi_0\rangle\langle\psi_0|$ pure and deterministic, and Convention \ref{conv:coupling}, for every $T>0$ there is $C_\ast=C_\ast(T,d,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty)$, independent of $N$, such that
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1}
			\sup_{t\le T}\ \mathbb{E}\big\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\big\rangle\ \le\ C_\ast,
		\end{equation}
		equivalently $\sup_{t\le T}N\,\mathbb{E} e_1(t)^2\le C_\ast$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Throughout, an operator carrying a slot index acts on that slot, the time variable is suppressed where no confusion arises, and $\varepsilon_j=\varepsilon_j(t)$. Since $\|\Psi_t\|=1$ and $\|\phi_{j,t}\|=1$ (Proposition \ref{prop:purity-N}, Lemma \ref{lem:reference}),
		\[
		\big\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\big\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\big(1-\langle\Psi_t,p_{j,t}\Psi_t\rangle\big),
		\]
		so it suffices to bound the drift of $1-\langle\Psi_t,p_{j,t}\Psi_t\rangle$, summed over $j$. Every coefficient below is bounded pathwise by a constant built from $\|L\|_\infty$ and $\|A\|_\infty$, since $|\mu^{(j)}_t|\le2\|L\|_\infty$ and $|\nu_{j,t}|\le2\|L\|_\infty$; consequently every local martingale appearing is a martingale, and $t\mapsto\mathbb{E}\langle\Psi_t,p_{j,t}\Psi_t\rangle$ is absolutely continuous with derivative equal to the expectation of the It\^o drift.
		
		\emph{Step 0: the It\^o expansion.} Write $a$ for the drift operator of \eqref{eq:vector-N} and $b_k:=L_k-\tfrac{\mu^{(k)}}2$ for its noise operators, so $d\Psi=a\Psi\,dt+\sum_kb_k\Psi\,dB_k$; and, on slot $j$, write $\tilde a_j$ for the drift operator of \eqref{eq:reference-vector} and $\tilde b_j:=L_j-\tfrac{\nu_j}2$, so that $dp_j=(\tilde a_jp_j+p_j\tilde a_j^\ast+\tilde b_jp_j\tilde b_j^\ast)\,dt+(\tilde b_jp_j+p_j\tilde b_j^\ast)\,dB_j$. The It\^o product rule for $\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle$ produces six groups of terms; the covariations of $dp_j$ with $dB_k$, $k\ne j$, vanish by independence of the noises, and the drift is
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1-drift}
			\Big\langle\Psi,\Big(a^\ast p_j+p_ja+\sum_kb_k^\ast p_jb_k+\tilde a_jp_j+p_j\tilde a_j^\ast+\tilde b_jp_j\tilde b_j^\ast+b_j^\ast\tilde b_jp_j+b_j^\ast p_j\tilde b_j^\ast+\tilde b_jp_jb_j+p_j\tilde b_j^\ast b_j\Big)\Psi\Big\rangle .
		\end{equation}
		Decompose $a=\sum_k\alpha_k-\tfrac iN\sum_{l<m}A_{lm}$ with $\alpha_k=-iH_k-\tfrac12(L_k^\ast L_k-\mu^{(k)}L_k+\tfrac14(\mu^{(k)})^2)$, and $\tilde a_j=-i(H_j+G_j)+\tilde c_j$ with $G:=\mathsf{B}(\eta_t)$ and $\tilde c=-\tfrac12(L^\ast L-\nu_jL+\tfrac14\nu_j^2)$; write also $c:=-\tfrac12(L^\ast L-\mu^{(j)}L+\tfrac14(\mu^{(j)})^2)$, so that $\alpha_j=-iH_j+c$ on slot $j$.
		
		\emph{Step 1: the slots $k\ne j$ cancel exactly.} For $k\ne j$ the operators $\alpha_k$ and $b_k$ commute with $p_j$, and their total contribution to \eqref{eq:A1-drift} is $\langle\Psi,p_j(\alpha_k+\alpha_k^\ast+b_k^\ast b_k)\Psi\rangle$. Since $\mu^{(k)}$ is a real scalar,
		\[
		\alpha_k+\alpha_k^\ast=-L_k^\ast L_k+\tfrac{\mu^{(k)}}2\big(L_k+L_k^\ast\big)-\tfrac14\big(\mu^{(k)}\big)^2=-\,b_k^\ast b_k,
		\]
		so this contribution vanishes identically, for every $k\ne j$ and every sample path. This is the number-conserving cancellation whose failure would produce $N$ terms of order one.
		
		\emph{Step 2: the local terms of slot $j$.} The free Hamiltonian cancels between $\alpha_j^\ast p_j+p_j\alpha_j=i[H_j,p_j]+c^\ast p_j+p_jc$ and the part $-i[H_j,p_j]$ of $\tilde a_jp_j+p_j\tilde a_j^\ast$; the mean-field part $-i[G_j,p_j]$ is deferred to Step 3. What remains of \eqref{eq:A1-drift} on slot $j$ is $\langle\Psi,\mathcal T_j\Psi\rangle$ with
		\[
		\mathcal T:=c^\ast p+pc+\tilde cp+p\tilde c^\ast+b^\ast pb+\tilde bp\tilde b^\ast+b^\ast\tilde bp+b^\ast p\tilde b^\ast+\tilde bpb+p\tilde b^\ast b,
		\]
		the slot index suppressed. Set $\delta:=\tfrac12(\mu^{(j)}-\nu_j)\in\mathbb{R}$, so that $\tilde b=b+\delta$ and $\tilde c=c-\delta L+\tfrac14\delta(\mu^{(j)}+\nu_j)$, and split $\mathcal T=\mathcal T_0+\mathcal T_1$, where $\mathcal T_0$ is the value at $\delta=0$. With $R:=c+c^\ast=-b^\ast b$ and the self-adjoint $S:=b+b^\ast=L+L^\ast-\mu^{(j)}$,
		\[
		\mathcal T_0=Rp+pR+b^\ast bp+pb^\ast b+\big(b^\ast pb+bpb^\ast+b^\ast pb^\ast+bpb\big)=S\,p\,S\;\ge\;0,
		\]
		since the first four terms cancel in pairs and the bracket is $(b+b^\ast)p(b+b^\ast)$. Thus $\mathcal T_0$ contributes to the drift of $\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle$ the nonnegative quantity $\|p_jS_j\Psi\|^2$, hence to the drift of $1-\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle$ a nonpositive one, and is discarded. Collecting the terms linear and quadratic in $\delta$ and using $bp+pb^\ast=Lp+pL^\ast-\mu^{(j)}p$, $b^\ast p+pb=L^\ast p+pL-\mu^{(j)}p$ and $\tfrac12(\mu^{(j)}+\nu_j)=\mu^{(j)}-\delta$,
		\[
		\mathcal T_1=2\delta\big(L^\ast p+pL\big)-2\delta\mu^{(j)}p .
		\]
		Testing against $\Psi$ and inserting $1=p_j+q_j$ next to $L_j$: since $p_jL_jp_j=\langle\phi_j,L\phi_j\rangle p_j$ and $2\operatorname{Re}\langle\phi_j,L\phi_j\rangle=\nu_j$,
		\[
		\big\langle\Psi,\mathcal T_1\Psi\big\rangle=2\delta\big(\nu_j-\mu^{(j)}\big)\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle+4\delta\operatorname{Re}\big\langle p_j\Psi,L_jq_j\Psi\big\rangle
		=-4\delta^2\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle+4\delta\operatorname{Re}\big\langle p_j\Psi,L_jq_j\Psi\big\rangle,
		\]
		whence $|\langle\Psi,\mathcal T_1\Psi\rangle|\le4\delta^2+4\|L\|_\infty|\delta|\,\varepsilon_j$. By \eqref{eq:dict-1}, $|2\delta|=|\operatorname{Tr}((L+L^\ast)(\Gamma^{(j)}-\gamma_j))|\le8\|L\|_\infty\varepsilon_j$, so
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1-local}
			\big|\big\langle\Psi,\mathcal T_{1,j}\Psi\big\rangle\big|\;\le\;80\,\|L\|_\infty^2\,\varepsilon_j^2 .
		\end{equation}
		This is the cancellation announced in Section \ref{sec:intro}: after the identities of Step 1 and $\mathcal T_0=SpS$, every surviving local term carries at least two factors of the excitation amplitude of slot $j$, and no term of order $\varepsilon_j^0$ or of order $\varepsilon_j$ alone survives.
		
		\emph{Step 3: interaction and mean field.} The remaining contributions to the drift of $\langle\Psi,p_j\Psi\rangle$ are $-\tfrac iN\sum_{k\ne j}\langle\Psi,[p_j,A_{jk}]\Psi\rangle$ from the interaction, only the pairs containing $j$ failing to commute with $p_j$, and $-i\langle\Psi,[G_j,p_j]\Psi\rangle$ from the mean field of the reference dynamics; together
		\[
		-\,i\,\big\langle\Psi,[p_j,X_j]\Psi\big\rangle,\qquad X_j:=\tfrac1N\sum_{k\ne j}A_{jk}-G_j=X_j^\ast .
		\]
		Insert $1=p_k+q_k$ on both sides of each $A_{jk}$ and use $p_kA_{jk}p_k=\mathsf{B}(\gamma_{k,t})_j\,p_k=\mathsf{B}(\gamma_{k,t})_j-\mathsf{B}(\gamma_{k,t})_j\,q_k$, which is the definition \eqref{eq:ops} of $\mathsf{B}$ evaluated at the pure state $\gamma_k$:
		\[
		X_j=\mathsf{B}\big(\bar\rho_j-\eta_t\big)_j+Y_j,\qquad \bar\rho_j:=\tfrac1N\sum_{k\ne j}\gamma_{k,t},
		\]
		\[
		Y_j:=\tfrac1N\sum_{k\ne j}\Big(-\mathsf{B}(\gamma_{k,t})_j\,q_k+p_kA_{jk}q_k+q_kA_{jk}p_k+q_kA_{jk}q_k\Big).
		\]
		Since $X_j$ is self-adjoint and $[p_j,X_j]=p_jX_jq_j-q_jX_jp_j$, the two commutator terms are complex conjugates under the expectation against $\Psi$, and the contribution is bounded by $2|\langle\Psi,p_jX_jq_j\Psi\rangle|$. We estimate the two parts of $X_j$ separately.
		
		\emph{The mean-field mismatch.} With $\Lambda_t:=\|\tfrac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\gamma_{k,t}-\eta_t\|_1$, Lemma \ref{lem:partial-trace} gives $\|\mathsf{B}(\bar\rho_j-\eta_t)\|_\infty\le\|A\|_\infty\big(\Lambda_t+\tfrac1N\big)$, so this part contributes at most $2\|A\|_\infty(\Lambda_t+\tfrac1N)\,\varepsilon_j$. This is the mechanism by which single excitations are created only through the deviation of the empirical reference mean from $\eta$; the deviation is the law-of-large-numbers quantity of Lemma \ref{lem:deviation}, and by independence of the reference filters
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1-lln}
			\mathbb{E}\Lambda_t^2\;\le\;d\;\mathbb{E}\Big\|\tfrac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\big(\gamma_{k,t}-\eta_t\big)\Big\|_2^2\;=\;\tfrac dN\,\mathbb{E}\|\gamma_{1,t}-\eta_t\|_2^2\;\le\;\tfrac{4d}N .
		\end{equation}
		
		\emph{The families with an excitation on slot $k$.} In the first, third and fourth families of $Y_j$ one factor $q_k$ can be moved onto the left vector, because $q_k$ commutes with $p_j$, with $q_j$ and with every operator not acting on slot $k$:
		\[
		\big|\big\langle\Psi,p_j\mathsf{B}(\gamma_k)_j\,q_kq_j\Psi\big\rangle\big|=\big|\big\langle q_k\Psi,\;p_j\mathsf{B}(\gamma_k)_j\,q_j\Psi\big\rangle\big|\le\|A\|_\infty\,\varepsilon_k\varepsilon_j,
		\]
		and identically $|\langle\Psi,p_jq_kA_{jk}p_kq_j\Psi\rangle|\le\|A\|_\infty\varepsilon_k\varepsilon_j$ and $|\langle\Psi,p_jq_kA_{jk}q_kq_j\Psi\rangle|\le\|A\|_\infty\varepsilon_k\varepsilon_{jk}\le\|A\|_\infty\varepsilon_k\varepsilon_j$. With the prefactor and the factor $2$ from the commutator, these three families contribute at most $\tfrac{6\|A\|_\infty}N\,\varepsilon_j\sum_{k\ne j}\varepsilon_k$.
		
		\emph{The pair-creation family.} The second family takes the reference product to a pair excitation and is the constraining one, since termwise it is only $O(\varepsilon_{jk})$ and there are $N$ terms. It must be summed before it is estimated. With $u_k:=q_kA_{jk}p_jp_k\Psi$,
		\[
		\Big|\tfrac1N\sum_{k\ne j}\big\langle\Psi,\,p_jp_kA_{jk}\,q_kq_j\Psi\big\rangle\Big|=\Big|\Big\langle\tfrac1N\sum_{k\ne j}u_k,\;q_j\Psi\Big\rangle\Big|\le\frac{\varepsilon_j}N\,\Big\|\sum_{k\ne j}u_k\Big\| .
		\]
		Expand the square. The diagonal terms give at most $N\|A\|_\infty^2$. In an off-diagonal term $\langle u_k,u_l\rangle$, $k\ne l$, move $q_l$ onto the left vector and $q_k$ onto the right one, each move a commutation with operators of other slots:
		\[
		\big\langle u_k,u_l\big\rangle=\big\langle A_{jk}p_jp_k\,q_l\Psi,\;A_{jl}p_jp_l\,q_k\Psi\big\rangle,\qquad
		\big|\big\langle u_k,u_l\big\rangle\big|\le\|A\|_\infty^2\,\varepsilon_k\varepsilon_l .
		\]
		Hence, by Cauchy--Schwarz over the labels,
		\[
		\Big\|\sum_{k\ne j}u_k\Big\|^2\le\|A\|_\infty^2\Big(N+\Big(\sum_k\varepsilon_k\Big)^2\Big)\le\|A\|_\infty^2\,N\big(1+\langle\Psi,\widehat{\mathcal N}\Psi\rangle\big),
		\]
		and, with the factor $2$ from the commutator, the family contributes at most $\tfrac{2\|A\|_\infty}{\sqrt N}\,\varepsilon_j\big(1+\langle\Psi,\widehat{\mathcal N}\Psi\rangle\big)^{1/2}$. The extraction of one excitation factor from each of two distinct slots in the off-diagonal terms is what carries the sum from the order $N^{1/2}$ of the termwise bound down to the order one required here.
		
		\emph{Step 4: Gr\"onwall.} Write $n(t):=\mathbb{E}\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle$; the product initial data give $q_{j,0}\Psi_0=0$ for every $j$, so $n(0)=0$. Summing the bounds of Steps 2 and 3 over $j$, discarding the nonpositive contribution of the $\mathcal T_0$-terms, and using $\sum_j\varepsilon_j\le\sqrt N\,\langle\Psi,\widehat{\mathcal N}\Psi\rangle^{1/2}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz,
		\[
		n'(t)\;\le\;80\|L\|_\infty^2\,n(t)
		+2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\big(\Lambda_t+\tfrac1N\big)\sqrt N\,\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle^{1/2}\Big]
		+\tfrac{6\|A\|_\infty}N\,\mathbb{E}\Big(\sum_j\varepsilon_j\Big)^2
		+\tfrac{2\|A\|_\infty}{\sqrt N}\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_j\varepsilon_j\,\big(1+\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle\big)^{1/2}\Big]
		\]
		almost everywhere on $[0,T]$, where $\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle$ abbreviates $\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle$. By \eqref{eq:A1-lln} and Cauchy--Schwarz the second term is at most $2\|A\|_\infty(2\sqrt d+1)\,n(t)^{1/2}\le\|A\|_\infty(2\sqrt d+1)(n(t)+1)$; the third is at most $6\|A\|_\infty\,n(t)$; and the fourth is at most $2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\big[\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle^{1/2}(1+\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle)^{1/2}\big]\le2\|A\|_\infty(n(t)+1)$, using $x^{1/2}(1+x)^{1/2}\le1+x$. Hence $n'(t)\le K(n(t)+1)$ with $K=K(d,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty)$ independent of $N$ and $t$, and Gr\"onwall's lemma gives $n(t)\le e^{Kt}-1\le e^{KT}$, which is \eqref{eq:A1}. The identity $\mathbb{E}\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle=N\,\mathbb{E} e_1(t)^2$ is \eqref{eq:e-number}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->

Summing the bounds of Steps 2 and 3 over $j$, discarding the nonpositive contribution of the $\mathcal T_0$-terms, and using $\sum_j\varepsilon_j\le\sqrt N\,\langle\Psi,\widehat{\mathcal N}\Psi\rangle^{1/2}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz,
		\[
		n'(t)\;\le\;80\|L\|_\infty^2\,n(t)
		+2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\big(\Lambda_t+\tfrac1N\big)\sqrt N\,\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle^{1/2}\Big]
		+\tfrac{6\|A\|_\infty}N\,\mathbb{E}\Big(\sum_j\varepsilon_j\Big)^2
		+\tfrac{2\|A\|_\infty}{\sqrt N}\,\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_j\varepsilon_j\,\big(1+\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle\big)^{1/2}\Big]
		\]
		almost everywhere on $[0,T]$, where $\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle$ abbreviates $\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle$. By \eqref{eq:A1-lln} and Cauchy--Schwarz the second term is at most $2\|A\|_\infty(2\sqrt d+1)\,n(t)^{1/2}\le\|A\|_\infty(2\sqrt d+1)(n(t)+1)$; the third is at most $6\|A\|_\infty\,n(t)$; and the fourth is at most $2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\big[\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle^{1/2}(1+\langle\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\rangle)^{1/2}\big]\le2\|A\|_\infty(n(t)+1)$, using $x^{1/2}(1+x)^{1/2}\le1+x$. Hence $n'(t)\le K(n(t)+1)$ with $K=K(d,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty)$ independent of $N$ and $t$, and Gr\"onwall's lemma gives $n(t)\le e^{Kt}-1\le e^{KT}$, which is \eqref{eq:A1}. The identity $\mathbb{E}\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\rangle=N\,\mathbb{E} e_1(t)^2$ is \eqref{eq:e-number}.
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
\label{rem:A1-mechanisms}
		Both cancellation mechanisms of the proof are forced by the case $A=0$, in which $\Psi=\bigotimes_k\phi_k$ up to a phase and every local and It\^o mechanism is already present: there Steps 1 and 2 must, and do, produce zero exactly. The two quantitative inputs beyond the algebra are Lemma \ref{lem:deviation}, entering through \eqref{eq:A1-lln}, and the two-slot extraction in the pair-creation family, which is the diffusive-measurement counterpart of the corresponding step in the closed-system counting arguments of \cite{Pickl2011,KnowlesPickl2010}. The bound sharpens the estimate behind \eqref{eq:KP-rate-trace}: it gives $\mathbb{E}\,\alpha_{N,j}(t)=\mathbb{E} e_1(t)^2=O(N^{-1})$, hence $\mathbb{E}\|\Gamma^{(j)}_t-\gamma_{j,t}\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$, the mean-field order.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- hypothesis-1: body_md -->
\label{hyp:A}
		There are constants $C$, independent of $N$, such that for all $N\ge3$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(A2)] $\displaystyle\sup_{t\le T}N^4\,\mathbb{E} e_1(t)^8\le C$ and $\displaystyle\sup_{t\le T}N^4\,\mathbb{E} e_2(t)^4\le C$;
			\item[(A3)] $\displaystyle\sup_{t\le T}N^3\,\mathbb{E} e_3(t)^2\le C$;
			\item[(A4)] $\displaystyle\sup_{t\le T}N\,\mathbb{E}\Big\|\sum_{j\ne1}\Delta^{(1j)}_t\Big\|_1^2\le C$;
			\item[(A5)] $\displaystyle\sup_{t\le T}N\,\big\|\operatorname{Cov}\big(\Gamma^{(1)}_t,\Gamma^{(2)}_t\big)\big\|_1\le C$;
			\item[(A6)] with $f^{(j)}_t:=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf A_0\Delta^{(1j)}_t)\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf B_0\Delta^{(1j)}_t)$, $\mathsf A_0:=A_0\otimes(L+L^\ast)$, $\mathsf B_0:=B_0\otimes(L+L^\ast)$, one has for all self-adjoint $A_0,B_0\inM_d(\mathbb{C})$
			\[
			\sup_{t\le T}N^4\big|\operatorname{Cov}\big(f^{(2)}_t,f^{(3)}_t\big)\big|\longrightarrow0,\qquad N\to\infty,
			\]
			the deterministic functions $\Sigma^N$, $\Sigma^{\mathrm{cr},N}$ of \eqref{eq:SigmaN}, \eqref{eq:Sigma-cr} converge in $C([0,T];\mathbb{R})$, and
			\[
			\int_0^t\Big(\sum_{j\ge2}\operatorname{Tr}\big(A_0\Theta^{(1j)}_s\big)\operatorname{Tr}\big(B_0\mathcal{M}[\Gamma^{(j)}_s]\big)-\Sigma^{\mathrm{cr},N}_s(A_0,B_0)\Big)ds\longrightarrow0
			\]
			in probability, uniformly on $[0,T]$.
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end hypothesis-1 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:rates}
		Assume (A2). Then, uniformly on $[0,T]$,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:rate-4}
			\mathbb{E}\big\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\big\|_1^4=O(N^{-4}).
		\end{equation}
		Under (A2)--(A3), and also unconditionally by Corollary \ref{cor:rates-uncond},
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:rate-3body}
			\mathbb{E}\big\|\Delta^{(123)}_t\big\|_1^2=O(N^{-3}),
		\end{equation}
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:rate-R}
			\mathbb{E}\big\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\big\|_1^2=O(N^{-2}).
		\end{equation}
		Unconditionally, by Theorem \ref{thm:A1},
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:F-moment}
			\mathbb{E}\big\|F^N_t\big\|_1^2\le16\,\mathbb{E}\big\langle\Psi_t,\widehat{\mathcal N}_t\Psi_t\big\rangle\le16\,C_\ast,\qquad t\le T,\ N\ge1,
		\end{equation}
		and $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:dict-2} and $(a+b+c)^4\le27(a^4+b^4+c^4)$,
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\|_1^4\le27\cdot64^4\big(\mathbb{E} e_2^4+2\,\mathbb{E} e_1^8\big)=O(N^{-4})
		\]
		by (A2), which is \eqref{eq:rate-4}; the same computation with the second power, using $\mathbb{E} e_2^2\le(\mathbb{E} e_2^4)^{1/2}$ and $\mathbb{E} e_1^4\le(\mathbb{E} e_1^8)^{1/2}$, gives \eqref{eq:rate-R} under (A2), and Corollary \ref{cor:rates-uncond} gives it with no hypothesis. For \eqref{eq:rate-3body}, square \eqref{eq:dict-3} and estimate the three types of term: $\mathbb{E} e_3^2=O(N^{-3})$ by (A3); $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_{12}^2\varepsilon_3^2]\le(\mathbb{E} e_2^4)^{1/2}(\mathbb{E} e_1^4)^{1/2}=O(N^{-2})O(N^{-1})=O(N^{-3})$ by (A2) and Cauchy--Schwarz; and $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_1^4\varepsilon_2^4]\le\mathbb{E} e_1^8=O(N^{-4})$.
		
		For \eqref{eq:F-moment}: $F^N_t=\sqrt N(\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\gamma_{1,t})$, so $\|F^N_t\|_1^2\le16N\varepsilon_1(t)^2$ by \eqref{eq:dict-1}, and \eqref{eq:e-number} converts the expectation into the excitation number. Finally $\varepsilon_{12}\le\varepsilon_1$, so by Theorem \ref{thm:A1}, $\mathbb{E} e_2\le\mathbb{E} e_1\le(\mathbb{E} e_1^2)^{1/2}=O(N^{-1/2})$ and \eqref{eq:dict-2} gives $\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
\label{rem:rate-source}
		The bound \eqref{eq:F-moment} identifies the analytic content of the central limit scaling: $F^N$ is, to leading order, the single-slot excitation amplitude of $\Psi_t$ against the moving reference $\bigotimes_j\phi_{j,t}$, rescaled by $\sqrt N$, and its second moment is bounded when the mean excitation number is. It is obtained with no Gr\"onwall argument and no chaos estimate.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:G-moment}
		Unconditionally, $\sup_N\sup_{t\le T}\mathbb{E}\|\widehat{G}^N_t\|_1^2\le32C_\ast+8d<\infty$; and, by Corollary \ref{cor:rates-uncond}, also unconditionally, $\sup_{t\le T}\mathbb{E}\|\varrho_N(t)\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$ and $\sup_{t\le T}\mathbb{E}\|r^{(1)}_N(t)\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
The first statement is Lemma \ref{lem:deviation} together with Theorem \ref{thm:A1}. For the remainders, insert the first statement and $\sqrt N\,\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\|_1=O(N^{-1/2})$, which follows from \eqref{eq:rate-R} and Jensen's inequality, into the bounds of Propositions \ref{prop:G-decomp} and \ref{prop:F-decomp}, using exchangeability in law for the sums over pairs.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rem:counting}
		The first moments \eqref{eq:e-number} are moments of $\widehat{\mathcal N}$, and all of them are bounded uniformly in $N$: this is Theorem \ref{thm:allmom}, proved in Section \ref{sec:moments} by iterating the mechanism of Theorem \ref{thm:A1} over the whole family of diagonal excitation observables. Clause (A3) follows (Corollary \ref{cor:A3}), as does every moment of a product of excitation observables over distinct label sets (Theorem \ref{thm:products}), and with these the rates \eqref{eq:rate-3body} and \eqref{eq:rate-R}. What moments of $\widehat{\mathcal N}$ do not give is a moment with a repeated label set: $\mathbb{E} e_2(t)^4=\tfrac1{N(N-1)}\mathbb{E}\sum_{i\ne j}\langle q_iq_j\rangle^2$, and moments of $\widehat{\mathcal N}$ control $\sum_{i\ne j}\langle q_iq_j\rangle$ only in $\ell^1$ over the $\sim N^2$ pairs, whereas the required $O(N^{-4})$ is an $\ell^2$ statement, equivalent to the excitation weight being spread over the pairs rather than concentrated on a few of them. Subsection \ref{ssec:tower} reduces this to an exponential moment of $\widehat{\mathcal N}$, which Subsection \ref{ssec:randrate} supplies on every horizon.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:chaos}
		For pure product initial data, unconditionally,
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:chaos-half}
			\sup_{t\le T}\big\|\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\eta_t\big\|_1=O(N^{-1/2}).
		\end{equation}
		If in addition (A5) holds, then
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:chaos-sharp}
			\sup_{t\le T}\big\|\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\eta_t\big\|_1\le\frac CN,\qquad
			\sup_{t\le T}\big\|\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(2,3)}_t-\eta_t\otimes\eta_t\big\|_1\le\frac CN,
		\end{equation}
		with $C=C(T,d,\|H\|_\infty,\|L\|_\infty,\|A\|_\infty)$, the mean-field order. The proof uses clause (A2) only through \eqref{eq:rate-R}, which is unconditional by Corollary \ref{cor:rates-uncond}.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
\emph{Step 1: the mean equation.} All coefficients are bounded on $\mathcal S$, so the stochastic integrals in \eqref{eq:reduced-sde} are martingales, and by \eqref{eq:reduced-drift}
		\[
		\frac d{dt}\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t=-i\big[H,\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]+\mathcal{D}\,\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t-i\tfrac{N-1}N\,\mathbb{E}\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]-\tfrac iN\sum_{j\ge2}\mathbb{E}\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[A,\Delta^{(1j)}_t\big].
		\]
		
		\emph{Step 2: the error sources.} The map $Z\mapsto\Phi(Z)$ determined on product elements by $\Phi(u\otimes v)=[\mathsf{B}(u),v]$ is linear on the finite-dimensional space $M_{d^2}(\mathbb{C})$, so there is $c_A=c(d)\|A\|_\infty$ with $\|\Phi(Z)\|_1\le c_A\|Z\|_1$; and $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{B}(X),Y]-[\mathsf{B}(\mathbb{E} X),\mathbb{E} Y]=\Phi(\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y))$. Since $\operatorname{Cov}(\Gamma^{\ne1},\Gamma^{(1)})=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{j\ge2}\operatorname{Cov}(\Gamma^{(j)},\Gamma^{(1)})$, clause (A5) bounds this term by $c_AC/N$. Without (A5), decompose, using the independence of $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$,
		\[
		\operatorname{Cov}\big(\Gamma^{(1)},\Gamma^{(2)}\big)=\operatorname{Cov}\big(\Gamma^{(1)}-\gamma_1,\Gamma^{(2)}-\gamma_2\big)+\operatorname{Cov}\big(\gamma_1,\Gamma^{(2)}-\gamma_2\big)+\operatorname{Cov}\big(\Gamma^{(1)}-\gamma_1,\gamma_2\big);
		\]
		the first term is bounded by $16\,\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2]\le16\,\mathbb{E} e_1^2=O(N^{-1})$ by \eqref{eq:dict-1} and Theorem \ref{thm:A1}, and the two cross terms by $O(1)\cdot O(N^{-1/2})=O(N^{-1/2})$ by Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{eq:dict-1}. By exchangeability in law $\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{\ne1}_t=\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t$. The prefactor discrepancy contributes $|\tfrac{N-1}N-1|\cdot2\|A\|_\infty\le2\|A\|_\infty/N$, and by Lemma \ref{lem:partial-trace},
		\[
		\Big\|\tfrac1N\sum_{j\ge2}\mathbb{E}\operatorname{Tr}_2[A,\Delta^{(1j)}_t]\Big\|_1\le\tfrac{N-1}N\,2\|A\|_\infty\,\mathbb{E}\big\|\Delta^{(12)}_t\big\|_1,
		\]
		which is $O(N^{-1})$ by \eqref{eq:rate-R} and Jensen's inequality, and $O(N^{-1/2})$ under (A1) alone by Theorem \ref{thm:rates}.
		
		\emph{Step 3: Gr\"onwall.} Set $v(t):=\|\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t-\eta_t\|_1$. Subtracting \eqref{eq:hartree} from Step 1 and using $\|[\mathsf{B}(\rho),\rho]-[\mathsf{B}(\sigma),\sigma]\|_1\le4\|A\|_\infty\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$ on $\mathcal S$ together with Step 2,
		\[
		v(t)\le\int_0^t\big(Kv(s)+\varepsilon_N\big)ds,\qquad v(0)=0,
		\]
		with $K$ independent of $N$ and $\varepsilon_N=O(N^{-1/2})$ unconditionally, $\varepsilon_N=O(N^{-1})$ under (A5). Gr\"onwall's lemma gives \eqref{eq:chaos-half} and the first part of \eqref{eq:chaos-sharp}.
		
		\emph{Step 4.} Decompose
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(2,3)}_t-\eta_t\otimes\eta_t=\mathbb{E}\Delta^{(23)}_t+\operatorname{Cov}\big(\Gamma^{(2)}_t,\Gamma^{(3)}_t\big)+\big(\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(2)}_t-\eta_t\big)\otimes\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(3)}_t+\eta_t\otimes\big(\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(3)}_t-\eta_t\big).
		\]
		The first term is $O(N^{-1})$ by \eqref{eq:rate-R} and Jensen, the second by (A5), the last two by the first part of \eqref{eq:chaos-sharp} and $\|\eta\|_1=\|\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(3)}\|_1=1$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
All coefficients are bounded on $\mathcal S$, so the stochastic integrals in \eqref{eq:reduced-sde} are martingales, and by \eqref{eq:reduced-drift}
		\[
		\frac d{dt}\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t=-i\big[H,\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]+\mathcal{D}\,\mathbb{E}\Gamma^{(1)}_t-i\tfrac{N-1}N\,\mathbb{E}\big[\mathsf{B}(\Gamma^{\ne1}_t),\Gamma^{(1)}_t\big]-\tfrac iN\sum_{j\ge2}\mathbb{E}\operatorname{Tr}_2\big[A,\Delta^{(1j)}_t\big].
		\]
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
The map $Z\mapsto\Phi(Z)$ determined on product elements by $\Phi(u\otimes v)=[\mathsf{B}(u),v]$ is linear on the finite-dimensional space $M_{d^2}(\mathbb{C})$, so there is $c_A=c(d)\|A\|_\infty$ with $\|\Phi(Z)\|_1\le c_A\|Z\|_1$; and $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{B}(X),Y]-[\mathsf{B}(\mathbb{E} X),\mathbb{E} Y]=\Phi(\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y))$.
